claims_checked.claim: Itadakimasu is a common pre-meal phrase meaning humble receiving.
It is exactly a religious prayer for most speakers.
claims_checked.note: Article treats daily use as manners/thanks; religious overlap possible but not required belief.

claims_checked.claim: School lunch often includes a group itadakimasu.
claims_checked.note: Common elementary-school practice; wording/cues vary by school.

claims_checked.claim: Gochisousama is a common after-meal closer.
Visitors are required to say it.
claims_checked.note: Article: not required; appreciated if matching the table.

claims_checked.claim: Everyone in Japan says it at every snack.
claims_checked.note: Snacks, izakaya, solo eating often skip or mumble.

caveats_about_absolutes: Note regional, generational, and situational variation
